a: Everyone has a different sense of easy, moderate, challenging and difficult, so the grade on each walk is a relative indicator of the level of challenge. Few Scenic Rim walks are easy walks on graded trails. Most routes have uneven ground, ascents and descents and rocky sections, and some gradients are very steep. There is always plenty of time to complete a walk, so nobody needs to speed through or feel they are not keeping up.

q: How long is a day walk?
a: Distance doesn't necessarily tell you how long a walk takes. Unless a walk says otherwise, assume you'll be out in the bush for a full day.

q: What happens if the weather turns?
a: Every walk is subject to change on the day depending on conditions, at the guides' discretion. Conditions are usually stable through the walking season, so changes are rare. If a walk is changed, cancelled or postponed you'll have at least 24 hours notice, barring unforeseen circumstances.

q: I've never bushwalked. Can I come?
a: Yes. Beginners are welcome. If you've never walked rough tracks or up a steep hill in the bush the idea can feel daunting, and these walks are a chance to try something new in a supportive group with an experienced guide. Come on the first couple of walks and see if bushwalking suits you. Call Teresa first to pick a good starting walk.

There is no upper or lower age limit, but some walks suit some people better than others, especially with health issues, bad knees or very young walkers. If in doubt, get in touch before you book so Teresa can talk through your needs and experience. Under 18s need a parent or guardian to sign the booking form.

q: How do I book and pay?
a: Request your walks from this site or by email. Teresa confirms availability by return email, then sends the booking and medical consent form. Day hikes are paid in full 14 days before the walk by direct deposit or cash, with a reminder by text or email. Multi day walks and events take a $500 deposit per person, with the balance due 60 days before departure.

q: What's included on a day walk?
a: An experienced and qualified guide with Wilderness First Aid certification, emergency equipment including a PLB, a hot cuppa at lunch with a home baked treat, a gear list for the walk, and interpretation of the flora, fauna, geology and history of the place. Walks on private property sometimes carry a small cash fee for the land manager, shown against the walk.
Generally a maximum of eight to ten walkers plus guides. Hosted weekends run with six to ten guests and the Border Tracks traverse is limited to nine.

q: Do you keep the group together?
a: Yes. These are group hikes and natural history interpretation is part of the experience, so nobody gallops past the interesting bits. For safety you are expected to stay with the group. These are not races to a destination.
No. Drones are not permitted on any walk. They intrude on wildlife and on the enjoyment of others, and in some national parks and public places they are illegal.

For a day hike, cancel more than 8 days before the walk for a refund or a credit for another hike of the same value. Less than 7 days out, no refund or credit is offered, though hardship may be taken into consideration. For multi day walks the $500 deposit is not refundable but can be transferred to another tour within 12 months; 59 to 31 days out you forfeit the deposit and 50 percent of the tour price, and 30 days or less there is no refund. Cancellations must be in writing by email or letter, not by text.

q: Where do the walks start, and can I share the drive?
a: Each walk has its own meeting point, usually a trailhead within an hour of Boonah, sent with your confirmation. Car pooling matters more than ever, and with permission Teresa can connect you with others on your walk so you can share travel.

q: I have a disability. Can you help me get outdoors?
a: Being immersed in nature and learning about our earth is important for everyone, regardless of age or capacity. Where possible Horizon Guides supports access to nature based activities for people with disability, their carers, families and friends. Many places in the national parks have excellent access for wheelchairs and other support, and you don't have to go miles away to have an adventure. Get in touch to talk about what would bring you joy.
